solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fidget can be masterly

indicators.note: the letters of the first word can be made into a different word, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A restless person turns out to be capable of brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' tells you the letters of FIDGET can be rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterly performer shows great natural talent, which is what being highly talented means.

clue.text: Man provided inside track to better accommodation

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man

indicators.note: one piece is put within another

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a track
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A fellow on a railway line is heading toward nicer lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; the definition is a verb phrase, to improve housing.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrade a run-down district's housing for wealthier residents is to improve its homes.

clue.text: Quaker gets no sleep in the woods

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the name

parts.note: Elizabeth Fry was a famous Quaker prison reformer
O looks like zero, nothing
to sleep is to rest

explanation.surface: A Quaker goes sleepless out in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Fry, a Quaker, reformed British prisons; she and the Quaker chocolate-making family give this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Land covered with trees is called woodland or forest; the word names such wooded ground collectively.

clue.text: School report overturned

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a note is a brief written report

explanation.surface: A school's report card has been overruled.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known independent school in England.

clue.text: One time lover has been put out

definitions.meaning: a former sweetheart from years ago
read literally, a fire that has been extinguished is a burnt-out blaze of yesteryear

explanation.surface: A former partner is offended at being dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a flame that has been put out is no longer burning, so it is an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a past romantic partner; a fire extinguished is literally a blaze no longer alight.

clue.text: Tell one all we arranged and stop interfering

indicators.note: the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to share what the group has planned, then to back off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals rearranging TELLONEALLWE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leave something as it is and not meddle with it.

clue.text: Foreign money I examine from mendicant friar

parts.note: the franc was the money of France and other countries
to scan is to examine

explanation.surface: A begging monk receives a foreign coin to inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of St Francis of Assisi form an order of friars living by alms.

clue.text: Redhead enters a make- believe retreat

indicators.note: one piece goes into the others

parts.note: pretence, a sham
the head, or first letter, of red

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person steps into a pretend hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' looks like a ginger person but gives the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a religious retreat or hermitage, especially in India.

clue.text: Inclined to lose time in the denouement

indicators.note: losing a letter means taking it out

parts.note: tending means inclined or disposed

explanation.surface: Someone disposed to waste time while the plot resolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A denouement is the conclusion of a story, where its threads are resolved.

clue.text: Midday flight is restricted

parts.note: noon, abbreviated N
a flight is a kind of arrow made for distance shooting

explanation.surface: A lunchtime plane journey has limits imposed on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel but is an archery arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrow is limited in width or scope, so it is confined or restricted.

clue.text: Diplomat's daughter married

parts.note: an attaché is a junior diplomat at an embassy; the 's reads as 'has'

explanation.surface: An embassy official's daughter has got wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'has': the diplomat has the daughter beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attached is spoken for, in a committed relationship, as a wedded person is.

clue.text: Serious about attorney and creditor who united and made a living

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the others

parts.note: earnest means serious
DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: Solemn talk of a lawyer and a lender who joined forces and got by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means made enough money to get by, earned a livelihood.

clue.text: Remains calm

definitions.meaning: what is left over, the remainder
repose, stillness, a quiet break from activity

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the remainder of something; the other is repose or inactivity.

clue.text: The Guardian gets Albert a decoration

parts.note: the Guardian is a British daily newspaper
an albert is a watch chain, named after Prince Albert

explanation.surface: A newspaper hands a man named Albert an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Albert' looks like a person but is the watch chain named after Queen Victoria's consort; the Guardian is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked loops of coloured strips are hung as festive ornaments at parties and Christmas.

clue.text: Pat's drama demonstrates scoring system

parts.note: a pat is a gentle stroke; the 's reads as 'has'
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A play by someone called Pat shows how to keep score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a name but is a light touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, this method totals every shot taken over the round, rather than counting holes won.

clue.text: On the whole and taking everything together

definitions.meaning: in sum, considering all of it from beginning to end

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means from start to finish, in all respects; both clue phrases express that overall sense.

clue.text: A fellow well-versed and exuberant

parts.note: fluent means smoothly expert, well versed in a language

explanation.surface: A man who knows his stuff and is full of high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant can mean abundant or plentiful, flowing freely, as wealth does for the rich.

clue.text: Church in request that's improper

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another

parts.note: an indent is an official request or order for supplies
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church receives an unsuitable demand.
explanation.walkthrough: An indent is a British term for an official order for goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent behaviour offends propriety, so it is unseemly.

clue.text: Dunce on a golf break for innocent pleasure

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person enjoys a golfing holiday for wholesome enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a holiday but is the signal to rearrange DUNCEONAGOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes wholesome entertainment with nothing improper about it.

clue.text: Conflict on the sea, briefly gave enthusiasm

parts.note: a war is a conflict
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A naval battle at sea briefly stirred people up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To be warmed to something is to have been made keen; to warm someone is to stir their fervour.

clue.text: Strong drink may go over to college

indicators.note: turned over, so the two words read backwards

parts.note: can means may, is allowed to

explanation.surface: Brandy might find its way to a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses CAN GO to OGNAC, which follows the college abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This brandy from western France is a potent spirit.

clue.text: Youth finds benefit in climbing

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: a climb is an ascent
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A young person gets a kick out of going uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is everyday British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, a teenager between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Leave a sovereign in charge

indicators.note: the coin is placed within the fee

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L is the symbol for pound

explanation.surface: A monarch is left in charge while someone departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like a ruler but is the old gold pound coin; L (from libra) stands for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, to depart in haste.

clue.text: Drama about a biblical character

indicators.note: the drama goes round the single letter

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A play about a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Noh is a form of traditional Japanese theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament patriarch built the ark to survive the Flood.

clue.text: Ale brewed to be incorporated in menus for the king of Sparta

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are put inside the other word
brewing turns ingredients into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beer is added to the bill of fare for a Greek monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' makes ELA, and 'to be incorporated in' sets it in the bill of fare; 'menus' looks like the setting but is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend he ruled Sparta and was the husband of Helen of Troy.

clue.text: Bind the officer's present

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer; the 's reads as 'is'
in attendance, here

explanation.surface: A tricky spot: the commanding officer's gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means here, as in a roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind is to stick together, which is what things that hold fast to one another do.

clue.text: Edward returned to the vaults finding cracks

indicators.note: coming back means the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward
crypts are underground vaults

explanation.surface: A man named Edward goes back down to the cellars and finds fissures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' looks like a noun but is a verb: solves a code.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code is to work out its hidden message.

clue.text: Gather round shelter and keep quiet

indicators.note: the gathering surrounds the shelter, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: to sit is to meet in session, as a parliament or court gathers
a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: People assemble around a refuge and stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a blunt command to be silent, to stop talking.
